explanation: It is a traditional instrument of Aboriginal peoples of northern Australia. Players keep its drone going with circular breathing, breathing in through the nose while the cheeks push air out.

claims.text: The didgeridoo is traditionally made from a eucalyptus trunk or branch hollowed out by termites.
The alphorn, the pan flute and the shakuhachi are not made from termite-hollowed eucalyptus.
The didgeridoo is a traditional instrument of Aboriginal peoples of northern Australia.
Didgeridoo players use circular breathing, inhaling through the nose while pushing air out with the cheeks, to keep the drone unbroken.
